steps: Confirm proximal DVT with compression venous ultrasonography (D-dimer to help exclude when pretest probability is low).
Anticoagulate once confirmed: DOAC monotherapy (rivaroxaban or apixaban) first-line, or parenteral heparin/LMWH bridged to warfarin (target INR 2-3); warfarin not DOACs for antiphospholipid syndrome.

Treat at least 3 months; for first VTE consider extended/indefinite anticoagulation when there is no identifiable risk factor or a persistent risk factor (Harrison de-emphasises 'provoked vs unprovoked').
For cancer-associated VTE use LMWH or a DOAC (apixaban/edoxaban; avoid DOAC with GI cancer) and continue until cancer-free.
Compression stockings for symptomatic relief; check renal function for dosing; counsel on PE warning signs.

confirm: Unilateral leg pain/swelling/tenderness; risk-stratify (Wells), D-dimer if low probability, compression US confirms.
